MINUTES  OF A REGULAR  MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL  OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE

  Tuesday, September 7, 2021

1.  The City Council Meeting was opened to the public. In an effort to keep a safe environment and to minimize the
  spread of the COVID- 19 Virus, the City limited occupancy and required masking for those in attendance. To
  facilitate public participation  for those who did not wish to attend in person, the meeting was made available
  virtually.

2.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6: 30 p. m.
3.  Council  Members  present:  Mayor  Tim  Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Muir Davis
  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  Assistant to the City Manager JR Ranells
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Fire Chief Christopher Nigg
  Police  Chief  Nick  Paz

  Community Services Manager Yvonne Duran

4.  Pledge of Allegiance  was led by Mayor Hepburn.

 5.  Announcements  of  Upcoming  George May, La Verne Library Manager announced that as of August 10,
  Community Events  2021, LA County Library has eliminated fines for overdue books and materials.
  Past, present, and future overdue fines will no longer be charged. LA County
  Library is happy to a fine fee library as other libraries in the County and in the
  world.

7.  Public Hearing/ Establishing  Assistant City Manager Ranells reported on establishing terms and conditions
  Terms and Conditions for  for La Verne Firefighters' Association Members. He stated that the City has
  La Verne Firefighters'  been unsuccessful in reaching an agreement on a successor Memorandum of
  Association  Members  Understanding ( MOU) with the La Verne Firefighters Association ( LVFA). As a
  result, the City has followed the applicable impasse procedures in accordance
  with the Meyers- Milias- Brown Act( MMBA) as well as its Employer- Employee
  Relations Resolution. Since there has been no change in either party' s
  position, it is permissible for the City Council, to consider unilaterally
  implementing the terms and conditions of employment for LVFA members.
  Mayor  Hepburn  called  for public  comment on  this  matter.
   City Council Minutes, Tuesday, September 7, 2021, Page 3,

  There was one public comment at the meeting and a copy of the public
  comment is attached.

  The City Council was grateful they did not have to resort to fact-findings. They
  looked to moving forward with the La Verne Firefighters' Association.

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Crosby, and unanimously carried to
  unilaterally implement the attached terms and conditions of employment for
  LVFA members as outlined in the City' s Last, Best, and Final Offer( LBFO).

8.  Unexpired  Planning  Community Services Director Scherer reported on the Unexpired Planning
  Commission  Vacancy  Commission Vacancy Appointment. He stated that Planning Commissioner
  Appointment  Phil May resigned from the Planning Commission with less than one year left
  on his term. The Council last conducted interviews in June of 2020 for the
  unexpired term of former Planning Commissioner Wendy Lau, ultimately
  appointing Thomas Allison and identified candidate Jeremy Conrad as second
  selection should another seat become available. Mr. Conrad has reapplied for
  this vacancy, as well as seven other residents, which none had applied for the
  previous two recruitments. The Council may decide on how to proceed with
  the appointment.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There was one public comment at the meeting. ( To hear what was said during
  public comment, please visit the City' s website to view the archived Council
  meeting.)

  City Manager Russi responded to a question that was asked on this matter.
  To hear what was said during public comment, please visit the City' s website
  to view the archived Council meeting.)

  After a brief discussion by the City Council, they all stated they were in support
  of appointing Jeremy Conrad to the Planning Commission. They spoke about
  his involvement in the community and that he was selected by City Council as
  the second choice at the last Planning Commission recruitment.

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Lau to appoint Jeremy Conrad to the
  Planning Commission to serve the unexpired term of former Planning
  Commissioner Phil May or until June of 2022.

  The City Council thanked all the applicants for applying and for their
  willingness to serve their community. They directed staff to maintain their
  applications on file for future City Committee vacancies.

 9.  Christmas Morning Coordination Community Services Manager Duran reported on the Christmas Morning
  Committee  Coordination Committee.  She stated that the last few years, the City' s
  Christmas morning tradition has become a multi- department effort comprised
  of staff and volunteers. Staff is looking to create a formal Christmas Morning
  Coordination Committee much like the 4th of July Committee in order to
  streamline these efforts. The Committee' s main focus would be to ensure a
  safe and successful Christmas morning on December 25th for years to come.

  City Manager Russi thanked the La Verne Fire Department who traditionally
  ran the Christmas Morning tradition for many years, but now it has evolved into
  a multi- department  effort and  community volunteers.
   City Council Minutes, Tuesday, September 7, 2021, Page 4,

  Mayor called for public comment on this matter.

  There was none.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis and Council Member Carder both stated they would like
  to serve on the Christmas Morning Coordination Committee.

  It was moved by Crosby, seconded by Lau, and unanimously carried to
  approve the formation of a Christmas Morning Coordination Committee and to
  appoint Mayor Pro Tem Davis and Council Member Carder to serve as the
  Council  liaisons  on the Committee.

10.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Hepburn called for
  public comment and waited for staff to check for any public comment via
  telephone  communication.

  There were five ( 5) public comments at the meeting. ( To hear what was said
  during public comment, please visit the City' s website to view the archived
  Council meeting.)

  City Manager responded to questions asked during public comment by
  residents. ( To hear what was said during public comment, please visit the
  City' s website to view the archived Council meeting.)

11.  Council Comments  Council Member Crosby thanked everyone who attended the Council meeting
  and the badge pinning ceremony for Fire Chief Nigg. He stated he was
  pleased with Chief's Nigg mission statement. He reported on the Smudge Pot
  Football game between Bonita and San Dimas High Schools and the rally. He
  announced that the La Verne Little League Softball Team will be recognized by
  City Council at their September 20, 2021, meeting at 6: 00 p. m.
  Council Member Carder congratulated and welcomed Fire Chief Nigg to the
  City and that she looked forward to working with him. She announced that on
  Saturday, September 11, 2021, there will be a Cool Cruise Car Show in
  downtown La Verne. She thanked and commended the La Verne RSVPs for
  serving the community and volunteering at the Car Show.
  Council Member Lau suggested that residents should visit Hillcrest Homes Art
  Gallery which is amazing. She also reported on the Diversity, Equity, and
  Inclusion Committee ( Dei) honoring different segments and groups in the
  community in the coming year. She also reported on the University of La Verne
  Home Opening Football Game. She stated we live in an awesome community.
  Mayor Pro Tem Davis welcomed newly hired Fire Chief Nigg and stated he
  was looking fonvard to see what he brings to the community. He also reported
  on the Cool Cruise Car show and the Smudge Pot Football Game between
  Bonita and San Dimas High Schools. He stated he now Chairs the Pomona
  Valley Transportation Committee and for residents to join them at their zoom
  meetings.
   City Council Minutes, Tuesday, September 7, 2021, Page 5,

  Mayor Hepburn reported on the recent RSVP annual Barbecue event and he
  apologized that he was not able to attend. He commended and thanked the
  RSVPs for their service to the community and that the City could not do
  without them. His heart and prayers went out to the fallen military personnel
  who were killed in Afghanistan. He also reported on the Cool Cruise Car Show
  and other events being held. He urged residents to go and shop La Verne.
  He reported on Senate Bills 9 & 10 regarding Planning and Zoning Housing
  Development pertaining to accessory units.

12.  Closed Session  At 7: 48 p. m., the City Council recessed to meet in Closed Session for the
  following:

  Review of Hearing Officer' s proposed decision on an Employee Disciplinary
  Matter( Personnel Rule 5200 F) per Government Code Section 54957( b).

  At 8: 15 p. m., City Council reconvened to open session.  It was moved by
  Davis, seconded by Crosby to adopt Resolution No. 21- 67, rendering a final
  decision regarding appeal of discipline.

13.  Adjournment at 8: 17 p. m., in memory of Salvatore ( Chick) J. Campo, a long- time La Verne resident. Chick was
  born in New York in 1948 and moved to California in his early years. He was in the Air Force and he was
  schooled in electronics. He was a Field Engineer and Training Specialist for Rockwell International for 30 years.
  During his career at Rockwell International he worked on numerous projects such as the Space Shuttle, Lunar
  Excursion, Module Secret projects, Destroyer( Submarine Hunters), Special Electronics for Submarines Global
  Positioning, Satellite System Navigation Systems for Fast Attack, Trident Submarines, and Avionics Systems for
  BI- Bomber RASC Vigilante F- 111 Apache Helicopters. Chick was very active in the Community. He was an
  RSVP from 1996 to 2019, volunteering many hours. He also served on the Pomona Valley Community Services
  Committee; he was the founder and past president of the La Verne Computer Club, he taught computers in
  La Verne and San Dimas; and he was a long- time member of the La Verne Senior Citizens Advisory Committee.
  He participated and assisted the University of La Verne in the video productions of several senior programs. He
  called Bingo for the Cities of La Verne and San Dimas. He was a Reverend at Faith Walk Christian Church in
  Ontario. Chick was an awesome friend, family man and loved helping people. He will be solely missed by those
  who knew and loved him;

  There was a moment of silence in memory of the 13 US Service members killed in Afghanistan supporting
  Operation Freedom' s Sentinel.

  The City Council adjourned to Monday, September 20, 2021, at 6: 00 p. m., for Recognition Presentation of the
  La Verne Little League Softball Team.

To: City Council

  City of La Verne
  Re: Fire Department

  First, I have to ask rhetorically, " Who' s in charge of Fire Department?" And who has
  been in charge the last six years. The LVFD used to be a great organization.

  1. Accountability- The fire department reports to the City Manager and it is his chief responsibility
  since it is one of our two public safety departments. The other one is the police department
  which reports to the City Council. The problems in the department have all occurred during his
  watch. Retention and recruiting have both been unacceptable during the last four years. What
  has he done to solve the problems?  He should have added a second office at the downtown
  fire station to immerse himself into the problems. You can say this and you can say that but
  results are whaYs important. IYs how you rate a City Manager. It is a no brainer that the City
  Manager receives an " F" in his stewardship of the fire department.

  2. Morale- The morale within the fire department is at an all time low. How often has the City
  Manager meet with the rank and file, heard their concerns and initiated a program to address
  their concerns. From what I' ve heard this is another " F".

  3. Recruiting —Another failing grade. We are losing to many fire fighters. I have done some
  research and there is a fire academy class at MT. SAC as well as six other locations in
  Southern California. If I was the City Manager, I would personally go to every academy in
  Southern California, ask to interview every candidate in the top third of their class two weeks
  before graduation. Sell La Verne as a great place to work. Give them 5 years to get their
  paramedic certificate. We need fire fighters now.

  4. Retention- IYs time to offer a retention bonus to every new fire fighter and current fire fighter. If
  a new fire fighter works here for 6 years, give him a $ 100, 000 bonus. Give the same bonus to
  a current fire fighter to show how much we appreciate their service and tenure. I know thaYs a
  lot of money but uncontrolled turnover is even more expensive.

  Most of the City' s departments are pretty well run so why not have the City Manager spend half
  his time fixing the Fire Department? It is that important. Don' t let him assign it to someone else.
  Give him goals and a time frame. Did his last review address his performance in this area? You
  five have the responsibility. Remember iYs about accountability, in the past and in the future.
  IYs time for the City Council to take an objective look at how the fire department got so bad. You
are accountable to the citizens to do the hard thing and hold Mr. Russ' s feet to the fire. No pun
intended. I ask redundantly, Mr. Davis does your boss hold you accountable? Mr. Crosby, you' re in
education. Don't you hold those reporting to you accountable? Mayor Hepbum is in a different
situation but his customers hold him accountable. If they didn' t, he would be out of business. Why is
Mr. Russi given a free pass? He is accountable to you five.

  Sincerely,

  Bruce M. Becker
